workload_termination.startup: baremetal/startup_mb.s sets SP, calls main, stores main return value to MAGIC, then spins
workload_termination.timeout_condition: no marker before c < max_cycles loop ends
workload_termination.timeout_returncode: runner/perf wrapper reports 1; this is not the workload's main return value

finite_workloads.mem_seq: four finite size/rep phases; 57,344 words across write/read/copy, about 172,032 word memory operations plus finite tail reads

digest_semantics.commit_digest: initialized to FNV offset; on every accepted commit, hashes retired sequence number and complete packet fields (PC/insn/next PC, GPR/SP/NZCV, memory, exception, monitor, vector/FP effects); no cycles/wall time
digest_semantics.memory_digest: initialized to FNV offset; hashes only committed mem/mem2 address/data/byte strobe effects
digest_semantics.memory_effect_count: increments once per committed mem or mem2 effect
digest_semantics.marker_order: digest/effect accumulation occurs before MAGIC detection in the same tick, so a pass includes its terminal MAGIC store while a timeout generally does not
digest_semantics.equivalence_implication: different retired prefix lengths naturally produce different cumulative digests; memory_digest is not a final RAM snapshot

dynamic_acceptance.recommended: run both f0 and f1a of each selected pair to marker completion under identical image/config/source/tool provenance
completion_requirements: both marker return codes are zero
retired_insn, commit_digest, memory_digest and committed_memory_effects equal
if traces are enabled, every commit field and memory effect order equal through completion
dynamic_acceptance.common_prefix_option: Use runner --trace/perf_runner.py --trace; compare seq and every PC/insn/next PC, GPR/GPR2/GPR3/SP/NZCV, mem/mem2 address/data/strobe, exception, monitor and vector/FP field. Any first prefix mismatch is an architecture risk; equal prefix with one timeout remains unresolved until marker completion.
